sub_criteria.name: agentic system design
sub_criteria.text: Describes or evaluates an LLM agent that searches literature iteratively: query reformulation, multi-round search, citation-graph traversal, or crawling, rather than a single retrieval call.

sub_criteria.name: baseline search recall
sub_criteria.text: Reports how much of a target set a single-query or Boolean database search actually retrieves, giving a recall or coverage number the agentic systems can be measured against.

sub_criteria.name: benchmark construction
sub_criteria.text: Says how an evaluation set for literature search or deep research was built - where the gold papers came from, how queries were sampled, what the annotation protocol was.

sub_criteria.name: retrieval and reranking
sub_criteria.text: Contributes the retrieval or reranking method underneath: dense or hybrid retrieval, LLM rerankers, citation-aware ranking, or evidence on which component carries the gain.

sub_criteria.name: gains that fail
sub_criteria.text: Reports a replication failure, a weak or unbeaten baseline, benchmark leakage or construction that inflates scores, or a gain that vanishes under a different set or metric.

items.title: On Understanding, Identifying, and Mitigating Vulnerabilities in Agentic Large Language Models
items.abstract_600: Large Language Models (LLMs) have undergone a shift from stateless conversational interfaces to autonomous agents capable of multi-step planning, tool invocation, code execution, and maintaining persistent memory. When these agents operate with real-world privileges---calling APIs, modifying files, and querying databases---a compromised reasoning step can trigger unauthorized data access, irreversible state changes, or cascading failures, yet the security research community has not kept pace. items.abstract_600: Financial indicators are essential tools for transforming raw financial data into interpretable measures for various downstream tasks, such as valuation, risk assessment, and economic analysis. However, existing financial benchmarks largely focus on answer-level accuracy and often assume that relevant data are already provided, leaving the assessment of the intermediate process of indicator construction underexplored. items.title: MIND: Lightweight and Effective Memory Injection Defense for LLM Agents via Intent-Aware Information Bottleneck
items.abstract_600: Memory-augmented LLM-based agents are vulnerable to memory injection attacks: Agents may retrieve poisoned memory from attackers, which diverts their behavior from initial user intent and finally causes task failure. However, existing defense mechanisms either incur high computational cost or suffer from information redundancy in multi-turn contexts. items.title: HiEviDR-Bench: A Benchmark for Hierarchical Evidence Aggregation in Deep Research
items.abstract_600: Deep research requires models to retrieve, connect, and synthesize evidence from large-scale heterogeneous sources to answer complex queries and produce analytical reports. Existing benchmarks mainly evaluate final outcomes, such as answer correctness, report quality, or citation alignment, while providing limited visibility into whether evidence is correctly selected, linked, and aggregated into supported claims and conclusions. items.abstract_600: Vision-language models (VLMs) have made interactive digital museums increasingly feasible by connecting 3D digitization with natural-language artifact exploration. items.abstract_600: Lifelong continual learning remains an obstacle on the path to human-like intelligence. Modern transformers show sparks of intelligence with in-context learning. items.abstract_600: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems depend critically on how documents are chunked and searched. items.abstract_600: Deep Research agents powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) have exhibited extraordinary potential in automated paper writing tasks. items.abstract_600: LLM-based multi-agent systems have been widely adopted for knowledge retrieval and report generation, synthesizing known information through web search and textual reasoning. items.title: ViDR: Grounding Multimodal Deep Research Reports in Source Visual Evidence
items.abstract_600: Recent deep research systems have improved the ability of large language models to produce long, grounded reports through iterative retrieval and reasoning. However, most text-centered systems rely mainly on textual evidence, while multimodal systems often retrieve images only weakly or generate charts themselves, leaving source figures underused as evidence. items.abstract_600: Agent evaluation requires assessing complex multi-step behaviors involving tool use and intermediate reasoning, making it costly and expertise-intensive. items.title: Personalized Deep Research: A User-Centric Framework, Dataset, and Hybrid Evaluation for Knowledge Discovery
items.abstract_600: Deep Research agents driven by LLMs have automated the scholarly discovery pipeline, from planning and query formulation to iterative web exploration. Yet they remain constrained by a static, ''one-size-fits-all'' retrieval paradigm. Current systems fail to adaptively adjust the depth and breadth of exploration based on the user's existing expertise or latent interests, frequently resulting in reports that are either redundant for experts or overly dense for novices. items.abstract_600: The development of general-purpose agents requires a shift from executing simple instructions to completing complex, real-world productivity workflows. items.abstract_600: Deep research systems powered by LLM agents have transformed complex information seeking by automating the iterative retrieval, filtering, and synthesis of insights from massive-scale web sources.
